title: Los Angeles Trivia Night: Questions From the Basin
description: Los Angeles trivia night ideas for rooms from Echo Park to Long Beach: Dodgers and Lakers rounds, studio lore, freeway pacing, and a local round to borrow.
h1: Trivia Night Across the Los Angeles Basin
kicker: Sprawling city, small rooms, and ten questions about home.
poem: Los Angeles comes to you sideways, through a windshield. Jacarandas drop purple on the parked cars in May, June brings a gray lid of marine layer that burns off by noon, and in the fall the Santa Anas come over the passes and make everyone a little strange. The late light on the west side is what the studios came here for, and it still works for free.

People say nobody walks here, but everybody gathers. They do it in strip-mall rooms beside a taco counter, in Koreatown basements, in back rooms in Highland Park and Long Beach. A trivia night in this town draws screenwriters who know every Oscar winner, Dodgers fans who still replay Kirk Gibson's 1988 home run, and a transplant from Ohio who takes the geography round with suspicious calm.

It is a city full of people who came to perform, and most of them are doing it on a Wednesday for a room of twenty: the stand-up on a bar stage in the Valley, the cover band in Silver Lake, the quizmaster reading question seven into a microphone that crackles. When the scores are in, the drive home is a river of red taillights on the 101, and the Hollywood Sign sits dark on the hill.

sections.h2: Dodger Blue, Studio Lore and the Traffic Clause
paras: A Los Angeles room will forgive almost anything except a lazy movie round, so make it specific: filming locations, the Chinese Theatre forecourt, the Walk of Fame, which studio sits where. Sports split three ways at least (Dodgers, Lakers, and whoever is loyal to the Clippers or a college team), so keep questions historical and fair. Food is a gift here: tacos, Korean barbecue, the French dip, and a long argument about who invented it.

Start later than you think. Nobody crosses town before 7:30 on a weeknight, so a first round at eight lets the people stuck on the 405 arrive in time. Check for Dodgers home games and Lakers playoff nights, and expect a lighter room on Oscar Sunday.

sections.h2: A Town of Performers Who Need a Weeknight Crowd
paras: Los Angeles has more working performers than almost anywhere, and most of them are not on a screen. They learn the craft in small rooms: open mics in the Valley, improv theaters on a Monday, a songwriter night in a corner of Echo Park, a quiz host who has been reading questions at the same table for a decade. Those rooms are where careers start and neighbors in a spread-out city meet.

They only work if people come. Buy a ticket to your friend's showcase and turn up to trivia in a week when it is raining (which here counts as an event). If your part of town has no weekly quiz, the Los Angeles round below is ten questions anyone with a microphone can start with.
